Apply imālah in all dhawāt al-yāʾ for Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir. Dualise the nouns if you intend to identify (them).

# Commentary

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (شَفَا) have imālah (أَمِلْ) in dhawāt al-yāʾ (ذَوَاتِ الْيَاءِ)[206], whether verbs, nouns or particles (فِي الْكُلّ).

In the second half of the line, the author offers a way of identifying dhawāt al-yāʾ in nouns (asmāʾ). If one intends to recognise (إِنْ تُرِدْ أَنْ تَعْرِفَا) dhawāt al-yāʾ in nouns, then place the noun in its dual form (وَثَنّ الاَسْمَا).

[206] Those words in which the yāʾ forms part of the original word and ends with the pronounciation of an alif, whether the yāʾ is written or not e.g. الفَتَىّٰ, الزِّنَا, هَدَىٰ. 302
And return its (dhawāt al-yāʾ) verb to oneself (if you wish to indentify it), like الفَتَىّٰ, هُدَىٰ, الهَوَىٰ, اِشْتَرَىٰ, اِسْتَعْلَىٰ and أَتَىٰ.

# Commentary

If one wishes to indentify dhawāt al-yāʾ in a verb, then return its verb (وَرُدّ فِعْلَهَا) – the verb of the dhawāt al-yāʾ – to oneself i.e. to the first person (mutakallim).

Subsequently, the author presents three examples of nouns and three examples of verbs. الفَتَىّٰ, هُدَىٰ and الهَوَىٰ are nouns. In their dual form they are الفَتَيَانِ, هُدَيَانِ and الهَوَيَانِ. اِشْتَرَىٰ, اِسْتَعْلَىٰ and أَتَىٰ are examples of verbs. In the first person they become اِشْتَرَيْتُ, اِسْتَعْلَيْتُ and أَتَيْتُ. This indicates that these words are primarily with a yāʾ.

Examples of nouns which are with a wāw instead of a yāʾ are صَفَا and أَبٌ which become صَفَوَانِ and أَبَوَانِ in their dual form. Examples of verbs which are with a wāw are دَعَا and نَجَا which become دَعَوْتُ and نَجَوْتُ when in the first person.
And however (words appear on the scale of) فَعْلَىٰ or فُعَالَىٰ – with a ḍammah or a fatḥah – and those (words where) their script is with a yāʾ.

# Commentary

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah in the feminine alif (alifāt al-taʾnīth).[207] Words with the alif al-taʾnīth appear on the scale of فَعْلَىٰ, whether with a fatḥah, ḍammah or kasrah (وَكَيْفَ فَعْلَىٰ) e.g. مَوْتَىٰ, مَرْضَىٰ, بُشْرَىٰ, قُصْوَىٰ, سِيْمَا, ذِكْرَىٰ, or on the scale of فعَالَىٰ, whether its with a ḍammah or a fatḥah (وَفُعَالَىٰ ضَمُّهُ وَفَتْحُهُ) e.g. أُسَارَىٰ, سُكَارَىٰ, يَتَامَىٰ, نَصَارَىٰ.

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah in all those words, whether nouns or verbs, that end with an alif which is written with a yāʾ (وَمَا بِيَاءٍ رَسْمُهُ). Examples of these follow in the next line.

[207] The alif al-taʾnīth is an additional alif (i.e. it is not primarily part of the word) which occurs on the fourth letter or more, and indicates towards that which is feminine, whether literally or figuratively e.g. الٔاُِنْثَىٰ, الُّدُِنْيَا. Imam al- Shāṭibī explains how to recognise them: وَفِي أَلِفَاتِ التَّأْنِيثِ فِي الْكُلّ مَيَّلَا * ...
Like (in) حَسْرَتَّىٰ, أَنَّىٰ, ضُحًى, مَتَىٰ and بَلَىٰ, excluding لَدِىٰ, زَكَىٰ, عَلَىٰ, حَتَّىٰ and إِلَىٰ.

# Commentary

Examples of words written with a yāʾ given by the author are: حَسْرَتَّىٰ, أَنَّىٰ, ضُحًى, مَتَىٰ and بَلَىٰ.

Five exemptions are mentioned i.e. though they are written with a yāʾ, imālah will not be made in them: لَدِىٰ, زَكَىٰ, عَلَىٰ, حَتَّىٰ and إِلَىٰ.

They (Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir) make imālah in الرِّبَا, الْعُلَىٰ الْقُوَىٰ, and كِلَا(هُمَا). Similarly, (they will make imālah) in (those words) increased from the basic trilateral verbs, like (in) اِبْتَلَىٰ. وَكَيْفَ جَرَتْ فَعْلَىٰفَفِيهَا وُجُودُهَا * وَإِنْ ضُمّ أَوْ يُفْتَحْ فُعَالَىٰ فَحَصَّلَا

# Commentary

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah (وَمَيَّلُوا) in the following words: الرِّبَا wherever it appears, الْقُوَىٰ of Sūrat al-Najm: 5, الْعُلَىٰ of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 4 and (كِلَا) كَلَاهُمَا of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 23.

They will also have imālah in those words which are derived from the basic trilateral verbs i.e. thulāthī mujarrad (مِنْ ثُلَاثِي) – even though with a wāw – but are written with a yāʾ when they appear in their increased form i.e. mazīd (مَزِيدًا) e.g. بَلَىٰ –) اِبْتَلَىٰ اَلْأِعْلَىٰ,(دَنَىٰ - يَدْنُو) اَلْأِدْنَىٰ,(يَبْلُوْ or اَلْأِزْكَىٰ,(عَلَىٰ - يَعْلُو) اِسْتَعْلَىٰ or (زَكَىٰ – يَزْكُو) يَتَزَكَّىٰ.

[Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah] with the verse-ends of (sūrahs) al-Najm, Ṭāhā, ‚Iqraʾ‛, al-Qiyāmah, al-Layl, al-Ḍuḥā, al-Shams, Saʾala (al-Maʿārij), ʿAbasa, al-Nāziʿāt and al-Aʿlāʾ.

# Commentary

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah on the verse-ends (مَعْ رُوسِ آيِ) of 11 sūrahs: Sūrat al-Najm (النَّجْمِ), Sūrah Ṭāhā (طَهَ), Sūrat al-ʿAlaq (اقْرَأ), Sūrat al-Qiyāmah (القِيَامَةِ), Sūrat al-Layl (اللَّيْلِ), Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā (الضُّحَى), Sūrat al-Shams (الشَّمْسِ), Sūrat al-Maʿārij (سَأَلْ), Sūrah ʿAbasa (عَبَسَ), Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt (وَالنَّزْعِ) and Sūrah al-Aʿlāʾ (وَسَبِّحْ).[208] Thereafter, the author mentions those words in which only al-Kisāʾī (وَعَلِي) will have imālah in i.e. excluding Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir.

Al-Kisāʾī will have imālah in (أَحْيَا) أَحْيَا wherever it comes, but not when attached to a wāw (بِلَا وَاوٍ) e.g. فَأَحْيَاكَم, فَأَحْيَا بِهِ, أَحْيَاهَا. However, when it comes with a wāw, which is only in one place in the Qurʾān – أَمَاتَ وَأَحْيَا of Sūrat al-Najm: 44 – then Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will all have imālah in it.

At the end of the line, specific words that have imālah for al-Kisāʾī continues (وَعَنْهُ مَيِّلِ).

[208] It is well known that imālah will not be made at each and every verse-end of these 11 sūrahs because at some of them imālah would not even be possible e.g. ذِكْرِي in Sūrah Ṭāhā, خَلَقَ in Sūrat al-ʿAlaq, وَأَخِيهِ in Sūrat al-Maʿārij, كَثِيرًا in Sūrah Ṭāhā etc. Thus, imālah will only be made in these sūrahs at those verse-ends which will allow for imālah to be made. Note that in Sūrat al-Aʿlāʾ, Sūrat al-Shams and Sūrat al-Layl, imālah is possible at every single verse- end.

[Al-Kisāʾī will have imālah in] مَحْيَاهُمُ, تَلَاهَا, خَطَايَا, دَحَا(هَا), تُقَاتِهِ, مَرْضَاتِ –however it comes – طَحَا(هَا), سَجَىٰ, أَنْسَانِيهِ, وَمَنْ عَصَانِي, ءَاتَانِيَ – not (the one) of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام – and وَقَدْ هَدَانِي.

# Commentary

Al-Kisāʾī will have imālah in (مَحْيَاهُمُ) مَحْيَاهُمُ of Sūrat al-Jāthiyah: 21. This will exclude مَحْيَايَ of Sūrat al-Anʿām in which he will not have imālah.[209] He will also have imālah in (تَلَا) وَالْقَمَرِ إِذَا تَلَاهَا of Sūrat al-Shams, the different forms of خَطَايَا i.e. خَطَايَاكُمَ, خَطَايَاهُم, خَطَايَانَا, (وَدَحَا) دَحَاهَا of Sūrat al-Nāziʿāt: 30, حَقّ تُقَاتِهِ of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 102 مَرْضَاتِ,(تُقَاتِهِ) however it comes (مَرْضَاتِ كَيْفَ جَا) i.e. مَرْضَاتِ اللِه, مَرْضَاتِي, (طَحَا) وَالْأِرْضِ وَمَا طَحَاهَا of Sūrat al-Shams: 6.

In the second line above, more words which only al-Kisāʾī will have imālah in are mentioned: (سَجَى) وَالَّيْلِ إِذَا سَجَىٰ of Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā: 2 and (وَأَنْسَانِيهِ) أَنْسَانِيهُ of Sūrat al-Kaḥf: 63. This will exclude فَأَنْسَاهُ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 42.[210]

He will also have imālah in (مَنْ عَصَانِي) وَمَنْ عَصَانِي of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: 36. This will exclude وَعَصَىٰ آدَمُ of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 121.[211]

He will furthermore have imālah in ءَاتَانِيَ الْكِتَابَ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام: 30 and ءَاتَانِے اللُه of Sūrat al-Naml: 36 (آتَانِ), excluding وَءَاتَانِي مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام: 63 (لَا هُودَ).[212]

The last word mentioned at the end of these two lines is (وَقَدْ هَدَانِي) وَقَدْ هَدَانِ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 80. With the stipulation of ‚إِنَّنِي هَدَانِّي,‛قَدْ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 161, اِجْتَبَاهُ وَهَدَاهُ of Sūrat al-Naḥl: 121 and هَدَانِّي of Sūrat al-Zumar: 57 are excluded.[213]

Two additional words are mentioned for al-Kisāʾī in the next line.

[209] مَحْيَايَ will specifically be mentioned in line 288.

[210] In فَأَنْسَاهُ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah.

[211] In وَعَصَىٰ آدَمُ of Sūrah Ṭāhā, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah.

[212] In وَءَاتَانِي مِنْهُ رَحْمَةً of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah.

[213] In إِنَّنِي هَدَانِّي of Sūrat al-Anʿām, اِجْتَبَاهُ وَهَدَاهُ of Sūrat al-Naḥl and هَدَانِّي of Sūrat al-Zumar, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al- ʿĀshir will also have imālah.

[Al-Kisāʾī has imālah in] (وَ)أَوْصَانِّي (بِالصَّلَاةِ) and رُؤْيَايَ. Al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah in) الرُّؤْيَا while al-Dūrī ʿAlī (has imālah in) رُؤْيَاكَ, with هُدَايَ and مَثْوَايَ.

# Commentary

Al-Kisāʾī (لَهُ) will also have imālah in (أَوْصَانِ) وَأَوْصَانِّي بِالصَّلَاةِ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام: 31. This will exclude وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَا of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 132.[214]

He will also have imālah in (رُؤْيَايَ) رُؤْيَايَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 43, 100. This will exclude الرُّؤْيَا and رُؤْيَاكَ which is mentioned immediately hereafter.

Al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (رَوَىٰ) have imālah in (الرُّؤْيَا) الرُّؤْيَا of of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 43, Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 105, Sūrat al-Fatḥ: 27 and Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 60 during waqf. Ḥamzah will not have imālah here.

Hereafter, all those words in which al-Dūrī ʿAlī (تَوَىٰ) specifically has imālah, are mentioned. They include: (رُؤْيَاكَ) رُؤْيَاكَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 5, (مَعْ هُدَايَ) هُدَايَ of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 38 and Sūrah Ṭāhā: 128, as well as (مَثْوَايَ) مَثْوَايَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 23. By stating ‚مَثْوَاهُ,‛مَثْوَايَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 21 and مَثْوَاكُمَ of Sūrat al-Anʿām are excluded.[215]

[214] In وَوَصَّىٰ بِهَا of Sūrat al-Baqarah, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah.

[215] In مَثْوَاهُ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام and مَثْوَاكُمَ, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir will also have imālah.
[Al-Dūrī ʿAlī has imālah in] مَحْيَايَ, with ءَاذَانِنَا, ءَاذَانِهِم, الجَوَارِ, along with بَارِئِكُم and طُغْيَانِهِم.

# Commentary

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī will also have imālah in مَحْيَايَ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 162[216], (مَعْ آذَانِنَا) ءَاذَانِنَا of Sūrah Fuṣṣilat: 5, (آذَانِهِمْ) ءَاذَانِهِم which comes in seven places: Sūrat al-Baqarah: 19, Sūrat al-Anʿām: 25, Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 46, Sūrat al-Kahf: 11, 57, Sūrah Fuṣṣilat: 44 and Sūrah Nūḥ عليه السلام: 7. He will also have imālah in (جَوَارِ) الجَوَارِ in Sūrat al-Shūrā: 32, Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 24 and Sūrat al-Takwīr: 16. Furthermore, he will have imālah of (مَعْ بَارِئِكُمْ) بَارِئِكُم in both places in Sūrat al-Baqarah: 54 and (طُغْيَانِهِمْ) طُغْيَانِهِم wherever it appears.

[216] This excludes مَحْيَاهُم of Sūrat al-Jāthiyah that was mentioned in line 285.
[Al-Dūrī ʿAlī has imālah in] كَمِشْكَاةٍ, جَبَّارِينَ, with أَنْصَارِي, the derivatives of سَارِعُوا and an option (between imālah and fatḥ in) البَارِئُ.

# Commentary

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī will also have imālah in (مِشْكَاةِ) كَمِشْكَاةٍ of Sūrat al-Nūr: 35, (جَبَّارِينَ) جَبَّارِينَ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 22 and Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 130, (مَعْ أَنْصَارِي) أَنْصَارِي of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 22 and Sūrat al-Ṣaff: 22, as well as the derivatives of (وَبَابَ سَارِعُوا) سَارِعُوا i.e. وَسَارِعُوا of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 33, نُسَارِعُ لَهُم of Sūrat al-Muʾminūn: 56 and يُسَارِعُونَ wherever it comes.[217]

Thereafter, a few words are mentioned in which al-Dūrī ʿAlī has an option between imālah and fatḥ. The first word appears at the end of this line: البَارِئُ of Sūrat al-Ḥashr: 24 (وَخُلْفُ الْبَارِي).

[217] يُسَارِعُونَ comes in seven places: Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 114, 176, Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 41, 52, 62, Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ: 90 and Sūrat al-Muʾminūn: 61. 309

[Al-Dūrī ʿAlī has an option between imālah and fatḥ in] (فَلَا) تُمَارِ (فِيهِم), with فَأُوَارِيَ and يُوَارِي; (imālah) from him (in) the ʿayn (kalimah) of يَتَامَىٰ (due to the) recurring (imālah) taking place.

# Commentary

In (تُمَارِ) فَلَا تُمَارِ فِيهِم of Sūrat al-Kahf: 22, (مَعْ أُوَارِ) فَأُوَارِيَ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah and يُوَارِي (مَعْ يُوَارِ) of Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 31 and Sūrat al-Aʿrāf: 26, al-Dūrī ʿAlī will have an option between imālah and fatḥ.

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī will also have an option of imālah in the ʿayn kalimah of مَعْ) يَتَامَىٰ عَيْنِ يَتَامَىٰ عَنْهُ) i.e. يَتَامَىٰ comes on the scale of فعَالَىٰ, thus referring to the imālah of the alif after tāʾ since the alif following the mīm will have imālah because it is with a yāʾ.

Ibn al-Jazarī explains the reason for this imālah when he states ‚الاِتْبَاعُ وَقَعْ‛ (recurring imālah taking place): imālah takes place because of imālah i.e. due to the imālah in the lām kalimah, imālah takes place in the ʿayn kalimah as well.

Thus, if imālah does not take place in the lām kalimah of this word due to ijtimāʿ al-sākinayn e.g. يَتَامَى النِّسَآءِ, then no imālah will take place in the ʿayn as well.

In the next line, four additional words are given which follows this rule.
[Al-Dūrī ʿAlī has imālah in the ʿayn] of كُسَالَىٰ, and of النَّصَارَىٰ, likewise (in) أُسَارَىٰ and سُكَارَىٰ.

# Commentary

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī will also have imālah in the ʿayn of كُسَالَىٰ of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 54, النَّصَارَىٰ wherever it comes, أُسَارَىٰ of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 85 and سُكَارَىٰ of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 43.

As mentioned before, if imālah does not take place in the lām kalimah of these words e.g. النَّصَارَى الْمَسِيحُ, then imālah will not take place in the ʿayn kalimah as well.

Those who agree (with Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir in making imālah) are Shuʿbah (in) الْأِعْمَىٰ, both (places of Sūrat) al-Isrāʾ; Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī and Yaʿqūb (make imālah in) the first place (only). And (imālah) in سُوًى and (in) سُدَىٰ.

# Commentary

From this verse onwards, the author starts mentioning those Qurrāʾ who agree (وَافَقَ) with Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (شَفَا) in making imālah.

Shuʿbah (صَدَا) will make imālah of الْأِعْمَىٰ in both places (فِي أَعْمَىٰ كِلَا) of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (الاَسْرَىٰ): 72.

Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī and Yaʿqūb (حِمًا) will make imālah in the first one only (وَأَوَّلًا). With the restriction to Sūrat al-Isrāʾ حَشَرْتَنِي أَعْمَىٰ,(الاَسْرَىٰ) and يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ أَعْمَىٰ of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 124, 125 are excluded.

Imālah will also be made in (وَفِي سُوًى) سُوًى of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 58 and (سُدَىٰ) سُدًى of Sūrat al-Qiyāmah: 36. Those who make imālah in these two words, amongst others, are mentioned in the next line.
Shuʿbah with an option (makes imālah in) رَمَىٰ and بَلَىٰ. Ibn Dhakwān has an option (between imālah and fatḥ in) مُزْجٰيةٍ, يَلْقَىٰهُ (مَنْشُورًا) and أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ اللِه.

# Commentary

Shuʿbah (صُنْ) – with an option (خُلْفُهُ) – will make imālah in in (وَفِي سُوًى) سُوًى of Sūrah Ṭāhā and (سُدَىٰ) سُدًى of Sūrat al-Qiyāmah. He will also make imālah with an option of fatḥ in (رَمَىٰ) رَمَىٰ of Sūrat al-Anfāl: 17, and (بَلَىٰ) بَلَىٰ wherever it comes.

Ibn Dhakwān (وَمُتَّصِفْ) will have imālah with an option (اخْتُلِفْ) in (مُزْجَا) مُزْجٰيةٍ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 88, (يُلَقَّىٰهُ) يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنْشُورًا[218] of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 13 and أَتَىٰ أَمْرُ اللِه of Sūrat al-Naḥl: 1.

[218] Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī will read this as يُلَقَّىٰهُ مَنْشُورًا, as opposed to يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنْشُورًا, as Ḥafṣ would read it.

Hishām – with an option – (has imālah in) إِنَاهُ. Shuʿbah (has imālah in) وَنَئَا of (Sūrat) al-Isrāʾ, with an option (of imālah in) its nūn. Khalaf from Ḥamzah (has imālah in the nūn as well as the hamzah) in both of them (both sūrahs).

# Commentary

Hishām (لِي) with an option (خُلْفٌ) will have imālah in (إِنَاهُ) إِنَىٰهُ of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: 53.

Shuʿbah (صِفِ) will have imālah in the hamzah of (نَأَى) وَنَئَا of Sūrat al-Isrāʾ: 83 (الْاَسْرَا) without an option. He will have an option of imālah in the nūn (مَعْ خُلْفِ نُونِهِ). Thus, Shuʿbah will have two ways of reading: imālah in the hamzah alone, or imālah in both the hamzah and the nūn.

This will only apply to Sūrat al-Isrāʾ (الْاَسْرَا) and not to Sūrah Fuṣṣilat.

In both, Sūrat al-Isrāʾ and Sūrah Fuṣṣilat: 51 (وَفِيهِمَا), Khalaf from Ḥamzah (ضِفِ) will make imālah in the nūn as well as the hamzah. Others who join Khalaf from Ḥamzah are mentioned in the next line.

Al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (will also have imālah in the nūn as well as the hamzah in both sūrahs). In those (alifs) after a rāʾ, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (without an option) and Ibn Dhakwān with an option will have imālah. Ḥafṣ has imālah in ىٰمَجْرَهَا. In the first أَدْرَىٰ…

# Commentary

In both, Sūrat al-Isrāʾ and Sūrah Fuṣṣilat (وَفِيهِمَا), Khalaf from Ḥamzah (ضِفِ), al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (رَوَىٰ) will make imālah in the nūn as well as the hamzah.

As for Khallād, he will only make imālah in the hamzah.

In those alifs that come after a rāʾ (وَفِيَما بَعْدَ رَاءٍ), in verbs e.g. اِشْتَرَىٰ, تَرَىٰ, يُفْتَرَىٰ, or in nouns e.g. بُشْرَىٰ, ذِكْرَىٰ, القُرَىٰ, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī without an option (حُطْ) and Ibn Dhakwān with an option (مَلَا خُلْفٌ) will have imālah kubrā.

Ḥafṣ (عُدْ) will make imālah in مَجْرَىٰهَا of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام: 41 (وَمَجْرَىٰ).

At the end of this line, the first (وَأَدْرَىٰ أَوَّلَا) أَدْرَىٰ which comes in the Qurʾān is discussed. It continues into the next line.

[In the first أَدْرَىٰ+ Shuʿbah (has imālah without an option) and besides it (the first أَدْرَىٰ), along with يَا بُشْرَىٰ, he has (imālah with) an option. Make fatḥ, (make) taqlīl of it (يَا بُشْرَىٰ) or idjāʿ of it (يَا بُشْرَىٰ) for Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī.

# Commentary

Shuʿbah (صِلْ) will have imālah without an option in the first (وَأَدْرَىٰ أَوَّلَا) أَدْرَىٰ which comes in the Qurʾān, Sūrah Yūnus عليه السلام: 16. In all other places where أَدْرَىٰ comes – besides the first place (وَسِوَاهَا) – along with يَا بُشْرَىٰ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 19, Shuʿbah will have imālah with an option of fatḥ (اخْتَلَفْ).

In يَا بُشْرَىٰ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَتَفْ) will have three ways of reading: fatḥ (وَافْتَحْ), taqlīl (وَقَلِّلْهَا) and imālah kubrā (وَأَضْجْعْهَا).

Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl in (dhawāt) al-rāʾ and the verse-ends; and (in) those (verse-ends which end) with a hāʾ – excluding (the verse-ends) with a rāʾ – he has an option (between taqlīl and fatḥ).

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq (جِفْ) will make taqlīl in dhawāt al-rāʾ (الرَّا)[219], as well as the verse-ends (وَرُءُوسَ الْآِيِ) of the 11 sūrahs mentioned previously without an option.[220]

However, those verse-ends of the 11 sūrahs should not end with the pronoun ‚هَا‛ (وَما بِهِ هَا) e.g. ضُحَىٰهَا, تَلَىٰهَا. If it does end with a hāʾ, then Warsh via al-Azraq will have taqlīl with an option of fatḥ (يَخْتَلِفْ).

If the verse ends with a rāʾ e.g. ذِكْرَىٰهَا, then Warsh via al-Azraq will only have taqlīl i.e. without an option.

[219] Those alifs which are written with a yāʾ and come after a rāʾ, whether a verb e.g. اِشْتَرَىٰ or a noun e.g. ذِكْرَىٰ.

[220] Refer to lines 283-284.

With (an option of taqlīl or faṭh for Warsh via al-Azraq in) dhawāt al-yāʾ, with (an option) related (in) أَرَاكَهُمْ. Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (has taqlīl) of فُعْلَىٰ – however it comes – along with (taqlīl in) the verse-ends.

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq will also have taqlīl with an option of fatḥ in dhawāt al-yāʾ (مَعْ ذَاتِ يَاءٍ), excluding the previously-mentioned dhawāt al-yāʾ which comes at the verse-ends; in which he only has taqlīl. The dhawāt al-yāʾ for Warsh via al-Azraq would include all the afore-mentioned places in which Ḥamzah, al-Kisā’ī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir have imālah in.[221]

Warsh via al-Azraq will also have taqlīl with an option of fatḥ in مَعْ أَرَاكَهُمْ) وَلَوْ أَرَاكَهُم وَرَدْ) of Sūrat al-Anfāl: 43, in spite of it being with a rāʾ.

Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَدْ) will have taqlīl of the alif al-taʾnīth which comes on the scale of فَعْلَىٰ, however it comes (وَكَيْفَ فُعْلَىٰ) i.e. with a fatḥah e.g. نَجْوَىٰ, يَحْيَىٰ, with a ḍammah e.g. رُؤْيَا, مُوسَىٰ or with a kasrah e.g. سِيمَا, عِيْسَىٰ. He will also have taqlīl of the verse-ends (مَعْ رُءُوسِ الْآِيِ) in the previously-mentioned sūrahs.

[221] Ibn al-Jazarī does not mention it here, but in the Nashr three words are excluded: مَرْضَاتِي, مَرْضَاتِ, مِشْكَاةٍ, الرِّبَوٰا and كِلَاهُمَا. See al-Nashr: 2/50. In these words Warsh will not have taqlīl.

*Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī has taqlīl of فَعْلٰى, فُعْلَىٰ, فِعْلَىٰ and the verse-ends of the 11 sūrahs] with an option (of fatḥ in them as well), except (in) dhawāt al-rāʾ. Al-Dūrī Baṣrī (has taqlīl with an option of fatḥ in) أَنَّىٰ, يٰوَيْلَتَىٰ, يٰحَسْرَتَّىٰ and (in) مَتَىّٰ (an option) is also related.

# Commentary

Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī will have taqlīl in all those words on the scale of فَعْلٰى, فُعْلَىٰ, فِعْلَىٰ and the verse-ends of the 11 sūrahs with an option of fatḥ as well (خُلْفٌ), except in dhawāt al-rāʾ (سِوَىٰ ذِي الرَّا), in which Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī will only have taqlīl.

Thereafter, seven words are mentioned in which al-Dūrī Baṣrī (طَوَىٰ) will have taqlīl with an option (الْخُلْفُ). Four are mentioned in this line: (وَيْلَتَىٰ) يٰوَيْلَتَىٰ,(وَأَنَّىٰ) أَنَّىٰ, (يَا حَسْرَتَّىٰ) يٰحَسْرَتَّىٰ and مَتَىّٰ is also related (قِيلَ مَتَىٰ).

The remaining three are mentioned in the next line.
(Taqlīl with an option of fatḥ) in بَلَىٰ, عَسَىٰ and يٰأَسَفَىٰ are related from him (al-Dūrī Baṣrī); and from many, apply imālah (kubrā) in دُنْيَا for him (al-Dūrī Baṣrī).

# Commentary

The remaining three words related in which al-Dūrī Baṣrī (عَنْهُ نُقِلْ) will have taqlīl with an option are: (عَسَىٰ) عَسَىٰ,(بَلَىٰ) بَلَىٰ and (وَأَسَفَىٰ) يٰأَسَفَىٰ.

While Ibn al-Jazarī attributes these differences only to al-Dūrī Baṣrī in the Ṭayyibah, in the Nashr he relates it for the entire Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī: for both al-Dūrī Baṣrī as well as al-Sūsī.[222]

In the word (دُنْيَا) دُنْيَا, many (وَعَنْ جَمَاعَةٍ) transmit imālah kubrah (أَمِلْ) for al-Dūrī Baṣrī (لَهُ). Thus, in the word دُنْيَا, al-Dūrī Baṣrī will have three ways of reading: (1) taqlīl and (2) fatḥ because it comes on the scale of فُعْلَىٰ, as explained in the two verses before this; then he will also have (3) imālah kubrā as mentioned in this line.

[222] Al-Nashr: 2/53-54.

In the two letters of رَأَىٰ, Ibn Dhakwān, Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah kubrā in both letters without an option) while Hishām has a choice (between imālah in both letters, or fatḥ in both letters). And besides the first place (where رَأَىٰ appears), Shuʿbah has a choice (between imālah in both letters with an option of fatḥ). Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (has imālah in) the hamzah (only).

# Commentary

In the two letters of (حَرْفَيْ رَأَىٰ) رَأَىٰ i.e. the hamzah and the rāʾ, when not followed by a sākin e.g. رَءَا كَوْكَبًا, رَءَا أَيْدِيَهُم, رَءَاهُ, then Ibn Dhakwān (مِنْ), Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صُحْبَةٍ) have imālah kubrā in both letters without an option, while Hishām (لَنَا) has imālah in both letters with an option of fatḥ in both letters (اخْتُلِفْ). Besides the first place where رَأَىٰ comes (وَغَيْرْ الاُولَى) i.e. رَءَا كَوْكَبًا of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 76, Shuʿbah (صِفْ) will have imālah kubrā in both letters with an option of fatḥ (الْخُلْفُ). In the first place – in Sūrat al-Anʿām: 76 – Shuʿbah will only have imālah in both letters i.e. without an option.

Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حِفْ) will have imālah in the hamzah only (وَالْهَمْزَ) i.e. with no imālah on the rāʾ.

The remaining Qurrāʾ will read with fatḥ.

And رَأَىٰ with a pronoun, Ibn Dhakwān has an option (between imālah and fatḥ) in it (the hamzah alone) or (an option between imālah and fatḥ in) the hamz and the rāʾ. Apply taqlīl in both (the hamz and the rāʾ) for Warsh via al-Azraq in all (of رَأَىٰ however it comes: with or without a pronoun).

# Commentary

If رَأَىٰ comes with a pronoun[223] (وَذُو الضَّمِيرِ) e.g. رَءَاكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا, رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزّ, رَءَاهُ, then Ibn Dhakwān (مُنًى) has imālah in only the hamzah (فِيهِ), or imālah in both the hamzah and the rāʾ (أَوْ هَمْزٍ وَرَا), or an option (خُلْفٌ) of making fatḥ in both the hamzah and the rāʾ. Thus, Ibn Dhakwān will have three readings:

1) Imālah in the hamzah only.

2) Imālah in both the rāʾ and the hamzah.

3) Fatḥ in both the rāʾ and the hamzah.

Warsh via al-Azraq (جَرَىٰ) will make taqlīl in both the hamzah and the rāʾ (قَلِّلْهُمَا) of رَأَىٰ whether it comes with a pronoun or without a pronoun (كُلًّاً).

In conclusion, when رَأَىٰ is not followed by a sākin or a pronoun, then there are four different readings:

1) Imālah in both the rāʾ and the hamzah – Ibn Dhakwān, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir, Shuʿbah (without an option in the first place and with an option in the remaining places) and Hishām (in one of his two options).

2) Taqlīl in both the rāʾ and the hamzah – Warsh via al-Azraq.

3) Fatḥ in the rāʾ and imālah kubrā in the hamzah – Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī.

4) Fatḥ in both the rāʾ and the hamzah – Qālūn, Warsh via al-Aṣbahānī, Ibn Kathīr, Hishām (in his second option), Shuʿbah in one of his options (excluding the first place in which he only has imālah) Ḥafṣ, Abū Jaʿfar and Yaʿqūb.

[223] This is only found in three words which appear in nine places: رَءَاكَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا of Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ: 36, رَءَاهَا تَهْتَزّ of Sūrat al-Naml 10 and Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ: 31, رَءَاهُ of Sūrat al-Naml: 40, Sūrah Fāṭir: 8, Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 55, Sūrat al-Najm: 13, Sūrat al-Takwīr: 23 and Sūrat al-ʿAlaq: 7.

And (رَأَىٰ) before a sākin, make imālah of the rāʾ (only) for Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Ḥamzah. And during waqf, all (the Qurrāʾ stop) like (they would stop) elsewhere (i.e. when it is not followed by a sākin or a pronoun).

# Commentary

If رَأَىٰ comes before a sākin (وَقَبْلَ سَاكِنٍ) e.g. رَءَا الَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا, رَءَا الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا, وَرَءَا الْمُجْرِمُونَ, وَرَءَا الْمُؤْمِنُونَ, then Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صَفَا) and Ḥamzah (فِي) will make imālah (أَمِلْ لِلرَّا) in the rāʾ only during waṣl.

However, during waqf (وَقَفَا), then all the Qurrāʾ (الجَمِيعُ) will stop like they would stop elsewhere (وَكَغَيْرِهِ) i.e. stop like when it is not followed by a sākin or a pronoun.
Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī, al-Dūrī ʿAlī (both without an option) and Ibn Dhakwān with an option (make imālah kubrā in) the alifs before the kasrah of a rāʾ at the end (of a word), like الَّدِارِ and نَارِ.

# Commentary

From this line, those alifs which precede the rāʾ maksūrah mutaṭarrifah are discussed (وَالٔاَِلِفَاتِ قَبْلَ كَسْرِ رَا طَرَفْ) e.g. الَّدِارِ, نَارِ. Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حُزْ), al-Dūrī ʿAlī (تَفُزْ) – both without an option – and Ibn Dhakwān with an option (مِنْهُ اخْتَلَفْ), will make imālah kubrā in them.

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī has an option (of imālah or fatḥ in) الْغَارِ. Al-Dūrī ʿAlī (without an option) and al-Dūrī Baṣrī with an option (have imālah in) وَالْجَارِ. Shuʿbah, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī, al-Kisāʾī, Qālūn and Ibn Dhakwān (have imālah in) هَارٍ.

# Commentary

In (غَارٍ) إِذْ هُمَا فِي الْغَارِ of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 55, al-Dūrī ʿAlī (تَمّ) has imālah with an option of fatḥ (وَخُلْفُ).

In (وَالجَارِ) وَالْجَارِ ذِي الْقُرْبِىٰ وَالْجَارِ الْجُنُبِ of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 36, al-Dūrī ʿAlī (تَلَا) without an option and al-Dūrī Baṣrī (طِبْ خُلْفَ) with an option have imālah.

In (هَارٍ) جُرفٍ هَارٍ of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 109, Shuʿbah (صِفْ), Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَلَا), al-Kisāʾī (رُمْ), Qālūn (بِنْ) and Ibn Dhakwān (مَلَا) have imālah.

The two them (Qālūn and Ibn Dhakwān) have an option (of imālah in هَارٍ). And if it (the rāʾ) is repeated Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah without an option) while Ibn Dhakwān and Ḥamzah have an option (of imālah or fatḥ). Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl.

# Commentary

Qālūn and Ibn Dhakwān have an option of imālah (خُلفُهُمَا) in هَارٍ. Thus, Shuʿbah, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī and al-Kisāʾī have imālah without an option in it, while Qālūn and Ibn Dhakwān allow fatḥ as well.

If the rāʾ is repeated (وَإِنْ تَكَرَّرْ) with an alif between them (and the second rāʾ with a kasrah) e.g. الْأِبْرَارِ, قَرَارٍ, دَارُ الْقَرَارِ, مِنَ الْأِشْرَارِ, then Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حُطْ), al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (رَوَىٰ) have imālah without an option while Ibn Dhakwān (مِنْ) and Ḥamzah (فَوْزٍ) have imālah with an option (وَالُخلْفُ). The second option for Ibn Dhakwān is fatḥ. The second option for Ḥamzah is mentioned in the next line. Warsh via al-Azraq (جَوَىٰ) has taqlīl.

[Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl] of this chapter (the alifs before the rāʾ maksūrah mutaṭarrifah); (in) جَبَّارِينَ and وَالجَارِ (Warsh via al-Azraq) has an option (of taqlīl or fatḥ). If the rāʾ is repeated, (then) Khallād, with an option, and Khalaf (without an option) agree (with Warsh via al-Azraq in making taqlīl).

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl without an option in all the previously-mentioned alifs before the rāʾ maksūrah mutaṭarrifah, whether the rāʾ is repeated or not (لِلْبَابِ).

In (جَبَّارِينَ) جَبَّارِينَ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 22 and Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 130, as well as وَالجَارِ (جَارِ) Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl with an option (اخْتَلَفَا).

If the rāʾ is repeated (فِي التَّكْرِيرِ), then Khallād with an option of fatḥ (قِسْ خُلْفٌ) and Khalaf without an option (ضَفَا) agree with Warsh via al-Azraq (وَافَقَ) in making taqlīl.

Considering that imālah was mentioned for Ḥamzah in the line before this, the following may be extracted:

• Khalaf has two ways – imālah and taqlīl.

• Khallād has three ways – imālah, taqlīl and fatḥ.
Ḥamzah has an option (between taqlīl or fatḥ in) قَهَّارِ and البَوَارِ. Warsh via al-Azraq (has taqlīl without an option in) تَوْرَاة while Ḥamza and Qālūn have an option (of taqlīl in تَوْرَاة).

# Commentary

Ḥamzah (فُضِّلَا) has taqlīl with an option of fatḥ (وَخُلْفُ) in (قَهَّارِ) قَهَّارِ wherever it appears and (الْبَوَارِ) البَوَارِ of Sūrah Ibrāhīm عليه السلام: 28.

Warsh via al-Azraq (جُدْ) has taqlīl in (تَوْرَاةَ) تَوْرَاة wherever it comes. Ḥamzah (فَضْلٌ) and Qālūn (بُجِّلَا) have taqlīl with an option (وَالْخُلْفُ) in تَوْرَاة. The second option for Ḥamzah is imālah kubrā; this will be mentioned in line 321. The second option of Qālūn is fatḥ.

And however كَافِرِينَ (comes), Warsh via al-Azraq (has taqlīl in it). And make imālah (in كَافِرِينَ) for Al-Dūrī ʿAlī, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (both without an option) and Ibn Dhakwān with an option. And say: Rawḥ…

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq (جَادَ) has taqlīl in كَافِرِينَ, however it comes (وَكَيْفَ كَافِرِينَ); whether it is with lām al-taʿrīf or not, as manṣūb or majrūr.

Al-Dūrī ʿAlī (تُبْ), Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حُزْ) – both without an option – Ibn Dhakwān with an option (مُنَا خُلْفٍ) and Ruways (غَلَا) without an option have imālah (وَأَمِلْ) in كَافِرِينَ.

At the end of the line, Rawḥ is mentioned as having imālah. This discussion continues into the next line.
[And say: Rawḥ] is with them (in making imālah of كَافِرِينَ) in (Sūrat) al-Naml. Ḥamzah (has imālah) in خَافَ, طَابَ, ضَاقَ, حَاقَ and زَاغَ, not…

# Commentary

Rawḥ – like al-Dūrī ʿAlī, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī, Ibn Dhakwān and Ruways (مَعْهُمْ) – will have imālah in إِنَّهَا كَانَتْ مِنْ قَوْمٍ كَافِرِينَ of Sūrat al-Naml: 43 (بِنَمْلٍ).

Ḥamzah (فُضِّلَا) has imālah in the alif which appears as the ʿayn kalimah in 10 trilateral past tense verbs (وَالثُّلَاثِي); five are mentioned in this line: خَافَ, طَابَ, ضَاقَ, حَاقَ and زَاغَ.[224]

In these five, Ḥamzah exclusively makes imālah, whereas in the remaining five, others besides Ḥamzah will also have imālah.

At the end of the line, an exception is mentioned (لَا). This continues into the next line.

[224] This includes فَلَمَّا زَاغُوا of Sūrat al-Ṣaff: 5. 324

[And زَاغَ; not] زَاغَتْ. Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī with another option and Ḥamzah (without an option have imālah in) زَادَ and خَابَ. Hishām with an option, Ḥamzah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Ibn Dhakwān (all without another option have imālah in) شَاءَ and جَاءَ.

# Commentary

Ḥamzah will not have imālah (لَا) in زَاغَتْ of Sūrat al-Aḥzāb: 10 and Sūrah Ṣād: 63.

Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī with another option (كَمْ خُلْفٌ) and Ḥamzah (فِنَا) without an option will have imālah in زَادَ and خَابَ.

Hishām with an option (لِي خُلْفُهُ), Ḥamzah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (فَتًى) and Ibn Dhakwān (مُنَا) – all without another option – will have imālah in شَاءَ and جَاءَ.

Nine words have been mentioned thus far. The tenth word is رَانَ and comes in line 315.

He (Ibn Dhakwān) has an option (in making imālah in) الْإَكْرَامِ, لِلشَّارِبِيَنْ, إِكْرَاهِهِنّ, الحَوَارِيِّيَنْ, عِمْرَانَ, المِحْرَابَ when it is not majrūr; so (in) this and (in) the first زَادَ (in the Qurʾān) no option (in making imālah) occurs.

# Commentary

Ibn Dhakwān with an option (وَخُلْفُهُ) in making imālah in (الاَكْرَامَ) الْإَكْرَامِ of Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 27, 78; (شَارِبِينَا) لِلشَّارِبِيَنْ of Sūrat al-Naḥl: 66, Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt: 46, Sūrat al-Qitāl: 5; إِكْرَاهِهِنّ of Sūrat al-Nūr: 33; الحَوَارِيِّيَنْ of Sūrat al-Māʾidah: 11 and Sūrat al-Ṣaff: 14; عِمْرَانَ of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 33, 35 and Sūrat al-Taḥrīm: 12, and المِحْرَابَ which is not majrūr (غَيْرَ مَا يُجَرْ) of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 37 and Sūrah Ṣād: 21.

However, when المِحْرَابِ is majrūr (فَهْوَ i.e. مَا يُجَرْ), as in Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 39 and Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام: 11, as well as in the first زَادَ in the Qurʾān – of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 10 – Ibn Dhakwān has no option (لَا خُلْفَ اسْتَقَرْ) i.e. he will only make imālah.
Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī has an option (of imālah in) مَشَارِبُ. Hishām (has imālah in) عَيْنْ ءَانِيَةٍ, with عَابِدُونَ, عَابِدٌ of (Sūrat) al-Jaḥd.

# Commentary

Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī with an option (كَمْ خُلْفُ) has imālah in مَشَارِبُ of Sūrah Yāsīn: 73.

Hishām (لِيَهْ) has imālah in عَيْنْ ءَانِيَةٍ of Sūrat al-Ghāshiyah: 5. This will exclude وَيُطَافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِئَانِيَةٍ of Sūrat al-Insān: 15. Hishām also has imālah of عَابِدُونَ and عَابِدٌ of Sūrat al-Jaḥd (الْجَحْدِ) i.e. Sūrat al-Kāfirūn. By restricting it to Sūrat al-Jaḥd, وَنَحْنُ لَهُ عَابِدُونَ of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 138 is excluded.

(Hishām has imālah in عَيْنْ ءَانِيَةٍ, عَابِدُونَ and عَابِدٌ) with an option (of fatḥ). Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah in) the rāʾ of تَرَآءَى (الْجَمْعَانِ). Al-Dūrī Baṣrī with an option (has imālah in) النَّاسِ when it is majrūr. Al-Kisāʾī, Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Ḥamzah have imālah in رَانَ.

# Commentary

Hishām has imālah in عَيْنْ ءَانِيَةٍ, عَابِدُونَ and عَابِدٌ with an option of fatḥ (خُلْفٌ).

Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (فَتَى) have imālah in the rāʾ of تَرَآءَى الْجَمْعَانِ of Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 61 during waṣl. When stopping, they will have imālah in the rāʾ as well as the hamzah following it.

Al-Dūrī Baṣrī with an option (طَيَّبَ خُلْفًا) has imālah in النَّاسِ when it is majrūr (النَّاسِ بِجَرْ).

Al-Kisāʾī (رُدْ), Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صَفَا) and Ḥamzah (فَخَرْ) have imālah in رَانَ of Sūrat al-Muṭaffifīn: 14.

In ضِعَافًا, Khallād (has imālah) with an option and Khalaf (has imālah without an option); (in) ءَاتِيكَ in (Sūrat) al-Naml, Ḥamzah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah without an option) while Khallād (has imālah) with an option.

# Commentary

Khallād with an option (قَامَ بِالْخُلْفِ) and Khalaf without an option (ضَمَرْ) make imālah in ضِعَافًا of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 9.

Ḥamzah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (فَتًى) – with Khallād having an option (وَالْخُلْفُ قَرْ) – make imālah in ءَاتِيكَ of Sūrat al-Naml: 39 (آتِيكَ فِي النَّمْلِ).

Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir, Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (have imālah in) the rāʾ of the ‚openers‛ (of the sūrahs). Al-Kisāʾī, Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī and Shuʿbah (have imālah in) the hāʾ of ‚Kāf‛(hā-yā-ʿayn-ṣād i.e. Sūrah Maryām عليها السلام).

# Commentary

The author starts discussing those who make imālah in the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt, referred to as the opening of the sūrahs (الْفَوَاتِحِ) since the sūrahs start with them.

Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صُحْبَةُ), Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī (كَفْ) and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حُلًا) have imālah in the rāʾ (وَرَا الْفَوَاتِحِ) of الٓرٰ and الٓمٓرٰ.

Al-Kisāʾī (رَعَىٰ), Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَافِظَ) and Shuʿbah (صَفْ) have imālah in the hāʾ of Sūrah Maryām (وَهَا كَافَ) عليها السلام i.e. in the hāʾ of كٓهٰيٰعٓصٓ.

And below (i.e. after Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام), Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (all without an option), Warsh via al-Azraq with an option, and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (without an option have imālah in the hāʾ of Sūrah Ṭāhā). Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī (have imālah in) the yāʾ of (Kāf-hā-yā) ʿayn (ṣād); a few relate an option (of imālah in the yāʾ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام)…

# Commentary

وَتَحْتُ refers to the sūrah ‚below‛ i.e. after Sūrah Maryām عليها السلام; Sūrah Ṭāhā.

Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صُحْبَةُ) – all without an option – Warsh via al-Azraq with an option (جَنَا الخُلْفُ) and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَصَلْ) without an option will have imālah in the hāʾ of Sūrah Ṭāhā. The other option of Warsh via al-Azraq is taqlīl, which will be mentioned in line 321.

عَيْنَ refers to the ʿayn at the start of Sūrah Maryām عليها السلام.

Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صُحْبَةُ) and Ibn ʿĀmir al-Shāmī (كَسَا) have imālah in the yāʾ of (يَا عَيْنَ) كٓهٰيٰعٓصٓ.

At the end of the line, the author mentions that few (قَلّ) relate the option (وَالُخلْفُ) of imālah in the yāʾ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام. This discussion continues into the next line.

[A few relate an option of imālah in the yāʾ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام] for the third imam, but not for Hishām. (In) the ṭāʾ, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Shuʿbah (have imālah). In the ḥāʾ, Ibn Dhakwān, Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (have imālah). In ‚Yāsīn‛, Shuʿbah and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir…

# Commentary

There are few (قَلْ) that relate the option of imālah in the yāʾ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام for the third imam (لِثَالِثٍ) i.e. Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī. Thus, most transmit fatḥ for Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī here.

But not for Hishām (لَا عَنْ هِشَامٍ) i.e. many transmit imālah in the yāʾ of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام for him. Others also transmit fatḥ for him here.

Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (شَفَا) and Shuʿbah (صِفْ) have imālah in the ṭāʾ (طَا) of طٰهٰ, طٰسٓ and طٰسٓمٓ.

Ibn Dhakwān (مُنَىٰ), Shuʿbah, Ḥamzah, al-Kisāʾī and Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صُحْبَةُ) have imālah in the ḥāʾ (حَا) of حٰمٓ.

At the end of the line, imālah in يٰسٓ is discussed. It continues into the next line.

[In ‚Yāsīn‛, Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir+ al-Kisāʾī, Rawḥ and Ḥamzah (have imālah in ‚Yāsīn‛). Ḥamzah and Nāfiʿ, both with an option (have taqlīl in ‚Yāsīn‛). (In the) rāʾ, Warsh via al-Azraq (has taqlīl). Nāfiʿ (has taqlīl) with an option (in) the hāʾ and the yāʾ (at the start of Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام).

# Commentary

Shuʿbah, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (صَفَا), al-Kisāʾī (رُدْ), Rawḥ (شُدْ) and Ḥamzah (فَشَا) have imālah in the yāʾ of (يَسٓ) يٰسٓ.

The discussion regarding imālah kubrā in the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt ends here. Henceforth, those who have taqlīl are mentioned.

Ḥamzah (في) and Nāfiʿ (أَسَفْ), both with an option (خُلْفُهُمَا) have taqlīl in the yāʾ of يٰسٓ. The other option for Ḥamzah is mentioned at the start of this line i.e. imālah kubrā. The other option for Nāfiʿ – Qālūn and Warsh via both al-Azraq and al-Aṣbahānī – is fatḥ.

In the rāʾ of الٓرٰ and الٓمٓرٰ, Warsh via al-Azraq (جُدْ) has taqlīl.

Nāfiʿ (وَاذْ) has taqlīl with an option (اخْتَلفْ) in the hāʾ and the yāʾ at the start of Sūrah Maryam (هَا يَا) عِليها السلام. This should not be confused with the hāʾ of طٰهٰ – which is mentioned immediately hereafter – and the yāʾ of يٰسٓ which has already been mentioned.

And below (i.e. after Sūrah Maryam عليها السلام), Warsh via al-Azraq (has taqlīl) in the hāʾ. Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī has an option and Warsh via al-Azraq (without an option have taqlīl in) the ḥāʾ (of the ḥurūf muqaṭṭaʿāt). (In) تَوْرَاة, Ibn Dhakwān, Ḥamzah, al-Kisā’ī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī make imālah.

# Commentary

The hāʾ which comes ‚below‛ (وَتَحْتُ) i.e. in Sūrah Ṭāhā, Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl with an option. His other option is imālah kubrā, which was mentioned in line 318. Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī with an option (حُلًا خُلْفٌ) and Warsh without an option (جَلَا) have taqlīl in the ḥāʾ (حَا) of the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt. The second option for Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī here is fatḥ.

Here the discussion regarding imālah and taqlīl in the ḥurūf al-muqaṭṭaʿāt ends. Those not mentioned – Ibn Kathīr, Ḥafṣ, Abū Jaʿfar and Ruways – will have fatḥ. The author subsequently mentions miscellaneous words in which the Qurrāʾ have differences regarding imālah in them.

Ibn Dhakwān (مَنْ), Ḥamzah, al-Kisā’ī, Khalaf al-ʿĀshir (شَفَا) and Abū ʿAmr al-Baṣrī (حَكِيمًا) have imālah kubrā (مَيَّلَا) in تَوْرَاة wherever it comes in the Qurʾān. Those who have taqlīl in تَوْرَاة have already been mentioned in line 308.[225]

[225] Ḥamzah has two ways of reading تَوْرَاة: taqlīl (understood from line 308) and imālah kubrā from this line. Nāfiʿ has three ways of reading تَوْرَاة: Qālūn has taqlīl and fatḥ, Warsh via al-Azraq has taqlīl and Warsh via al- Aṣbahānī has imālah kubrā.
Besides it (besides تَوْرَاة, Warsh via) al-Aṣbahānī does not have imālah. Idrīs has an option (of imālah) in رُؤْيَا when (it is) not with ‚اَلْ‛.

# Commentary

Besides (وَغَيْرُهْا) تَوْرَاة, Warsh via al-Aṣbahānī (لِلٔاَصْبَهَانِي) generally does not make imālah.[226] Thus, al-Aṣbahānī has imālah kubrā without an option in تَوْرَاة wherever it comes.

Idrīs with an option (وَخُلْفُ إِدْرِيسَ) has imālah with an option of fatḥ in رُؤْيَاكَ and رُؤْيَايَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 4, 5, 100 (لَا بِأَلْ); without ‚اَلْ‛ i.e. not الرُّؤْيَا wherever it comes. Isḥāq will have fatḥ when it comes without ‚اَلْ‛. However, when it comes with ‚اَلْ‛, both Idrīs and Isḥāq will only have imālah. Refer to line 287.

This line terminates the discussion of all the words in which the Qurrāʾ have imālah. From the next line, the author discusses some matters pertaining to imālah.

[226] Bear in mind that line 308 relates taqlīl for al-Aṣbahānī in the hāʾ of كٓهٰيٰعٓصٓ and the yāʾ of يٰسٓ.
Idghām (kabīr) and waqf with a sukūn will not prevent imālah taking place due to a kasrah. And from…

# Commentary

Idghām kabīr (إدْغَامٌ) and waqf with a sukūn (وَوَقْفٌ إِنْ سَكَنْ) will not prevent (وَلَيْسَ...يَمْنَعُ) imālah – whether ṣughrā or kubrā – taking place due to a kasrah (مَا يُمَالُ لِلْكَسْرِ) e.g. الَّدِارِ, هَارٍ, الْأِبْرَارِ, النَّاسِ, فَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ * رَبَّنَا, كِتَابَ الْأِبْرَارِ لَفِي عِلِّيِّيَنْ.

At the end of the line, the practice for al-Sūsī is discussed. This goes into the next line.

[And from] al-Sūsī there is difference of opinion: some (relate that) taqlīl be made. And there is no difference of opinion raised in a word with a tanwīn. In fact, before a sākin, stop based on the principles layed down (for them). Al-Sūsī has an option (of imālah in) the likes of القُرَى الَّتِي during waṣl.

# Commentary

From al-Sūsī (وَعَنْ سُوسٍ) there is difference of opinion: some will make imālah, while others will make fatḥ during idghām kabīr and waqf with a sukūn. A few relate taqlīl (وَلِبَعْضٍ قُلِّلَا) for him as well. Thus, there are three ways for al-Sūsī:

1) Imālah kubrā

2) Fatḥ

3) Taqlīl

In the second half of the line the author explains that when stopping on a word with a tanwīn e.g. هُدًى لِّلْمُتَّقِيَنْ, قُرًى ظَاهِرَةً, there will be no difference of opinion between the Qurrāʾ in stopping according to their various applications (بِمَا أُصِّلَ قِفْ) i.e. those who apply fatḥ will have fatḥ, those apply taqlīl will have taqlīl, and those who apply imālah will have imālah.[227]

Likewise, if a word of imālah comes before a sākin (بَلْ قَبْلَ سَاكِنٍ) e.g. مُوسَى الْكِتَابَ, ذِكْرَى الَّدِارِ, then waqf will be made on the word of imālah according to the applications of the Qurrāʾ.

However, al-Sūsī (يَصِفْ) has an option (وَخُلْفُ) in the likes of القُرَى الَّتِي – dhawāt al-rāʾ before a sākin – during waṣl i.e. he will have an option of making imālah or fatḥ e.g. ذِكْرَى الَّدِارِ, نَرَى اللَه, سَيَرَى اللُه, النَّصَارَى الْمَسِيحُ.

[227] This is contrary to what Imam al-Shāṭibī mentions in line 337 of his Shāṭibiyyah. Imam al-Jazarī relates in his Nashr that none of the Qurrāʾ practice upon this; rather, it is a view amongst grammarians. See al-Nashr: 2/75. 334

It is related from him (from al-Sūsī, that imālah be made) before a sākin (in) the two letters of رَأَىٰ; (imālah in only) the rāʾ (of رَأَىٰ), and besides this (i.e. besides when it is before a sākīn) and (in) the hamz of نَأَىٰ.

# Commentary

It is related (وَقِيلَ) that al-Sūsī (عَنْهُ) has imālah of both the rāʾ and the hamzah of رَأَىٰ (حَرْفَيْ رَأَىٰ) before a sākin (قَبْلَ سَاكِنٍ) e.g. رَءَى الْقَمَرَ, رَأَى الشَّمْسَ.[228]

Similarly, imālah in the rāʾ (وَرَا) is related for him when it is not before a sākin (سِوَاهُ) e.g. رَأَىٰ كَوْكَبًا.[229]

They also relate imālah in the hamzah of (مَعْ هَمْزِ نَأَىٰ) نَأَىٰ for al-Sūsī.[230]

However, Ibn al-Jazarī has refuted all these applications mentioned in this last line for al-Sūsī in his Nashr.[231] Imālah of the Hāʾ al-Taʾnīth and what is before it during Waqf

The hāʾ al-taʾnīth is that hāʾ which comes at the end of a noun; read as a tāʾ during waṣl and as a hāʾ during waqf e.g. رَحْمَتْ of Sūrah Āl ʿImrān: 8, نِعْمَةَ etc.

The majority are of the opinion that imālah takes place in the letter before the hāʾ al-taʾnīth only, whereas others like al-Dānī, Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Mahdawī and al-Shāṭibī, argue that imālah takes place in the letter before the hāʾ al-taʾnīth as well as in the hāʾ al-taʾnīth. Ibn al-Jazarī regards this disparity between scholars as being a difference of expression in that imālah technically means the inclination of the fatḥah towards a kasrah and an alif to a yāʾ. While all, including al-Dānī, would agree that this does not take place in the hāʾ al-taʾnīth (in spite of al-Dānī and others holding this view). In addition to this, the majority will also concede that the imālah of the letter before the hāʾ will weaken the pronunciation of the hāʾ somewhat (in spite of them arguing that imālah only takes place in the letter before the hā al-taʾnīth).[232] And Allah knows best.

Ziyādāt al-Ṭayyibah:

Via the Shāṭibiyyah, two practices are mentioned for al-Kisāʾī. The one is that imālah is made before the hāʾ al-taʾnīth when it is preceded by any letter, except for the alif. The second practice is more intricate and divides the letters into three categories:

1) Those in which there is agreement that imālah will be made – this is found in the combination فَجَثَتْ زَيْنَبُ لِذَوْدِ شَمْسٍ.

2) Those in which there is agreement that no imālah will be made – this is found in the seven letters of istiʿlāʾ – خُصّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ – and the three letters of حَاعٍ.

3) Those in which imālah takes place in certain circumstances and in other circumstances it will not: the four letters of أَكْهَر when they come after a kasrah or yāʾ sākinah, then imālah will take place, or else fatḥ will be made.

The Ṭayyibah also holds these two practices.

Additionally, the Ṭayyibah includes ‚أَهْ‛ – the hamzah and the hāʾ – with the 10 letters in which imālah is prevented, irrespective of whether they are preceded by a kasrah or yāʾ sākinah e.g. فِئَةٍ, خَطِيٓئَةً, فَاكِهَةٌ,[233] or not. Thus, only fatḥ is allowed when the hāʾ al-taʾnīth is preceded by a hamzah or a hāʾ via this view in the Ṭayyibah.

In فِطْرَتَ of Sūrat al-Rūm: 30, the Shāṭibiyyah only has imālah. Via the Ṭayyibah, faṭh will also be allowed.

All the practices that are mentioned for al-Kisāʾi above are also related for Ḥamzah via the Ṭayyibah.

[228] Imam al-Shāṭibī suggests this for al-Sūsī in line 648 of his Shāṭibiyyah. However, Imam al-Jazarī has refuted this as an application via the Shāṭibiyyah, the Taysīr or via the ṭuruq of the Nashr. See al-Nashr: 2/47.

[229] Imam al-Shāṭibī suggests this for al-Sūsī in line 648 of his Shāṭibiyyah. However, Imam al-Jazarī has refuted this as an application via the Shāṭibiyyah, the Taysīr or via the ṭuruq of the Nashr. See al-Nashr: 2/45.

[230] Imam al-Shāṭibī suggests this for al-Sūsī in line 312 of his Shāṭibiyyah. However, Imam al-Jazarī relates that there is concensus amongst of the ṭuruq of al-Sūsī that fatḥ will be made for him here. See al-Nashr: 2/44.

[231] Likewise, Imam al-Jazarī also refutes imālah of the hamzah of رَأَىٰ when followed by a sākin for Shuʿbah, even though Imam al-Shāṭibī mentions a choice for Shuʿbah in his Shāṭibiyyah (line 648). See al-Nashr: 2/46-47.

[232] Al-Nashr: 2/88.

[233] There is no example of where the hāʾ is preceded by a yāʾ sākinah.
Make imālah for ʿAlī (al-Kisāʾī) in the hāʾ al-taʾnīth and what is before it, not when (the hāʾ al-taʾnīth comes) after (the letters of) istiʿlāʾ or the (letters of) حَاعٍ.

# Commentary

Al-Kisāʾī (لِعَلِي) will make imālah (مَيِّلِ) in the hāʾ al-taʾnīth (وَهَاءَ تَأْنِيثٍ) and what is before it (وَقَبْلُ) during waqf.

However, he will not make imālah when the hāʾ al-taʾnīth follows 10 letters: the seven letters of istiʿlāʾ – خُصّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ – and the three letters of (لَا بَعْدَ الاِسْتِعْلَا وحَاعٍ) حَاعٍ e.g. نَفْخَةٌ, خَالِصَةً, بَعُوضَةً, صِبْغَةَ, حِطَّةٌ, نَاقَةُ, مَوْعِظَةٌ, وَالنَّطِيحَةُ, الصَّلَاةَ, القَارِعَةُ.

The letters appearing before the hāʾ al-taʾnīth may be divided into three categories:

1) Those in which there is agreement that imālah will be made – this is found in the combination فَجَثَتْ زَيْنَبُ لِذَوْدِ شَمْسٍ.

2) Those in which there is agreement that no imālah will be made – this is seven letters of istiʿlāʾ – خُصّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ – and the three letters of حَاعٍ.

3) Those in which imālah takes place in certain circumstances and in other circumstances, it will not: the four letters of أَكْهَر, when they come after a kasrah or yāʾ sākinah then imālah will take place, or else fatḥ will be made.

The first two categories are outlined in this verse. The third category is mentioned next.
(ʿAlī will not make imālah in the letters of) أَكْهَر, except (when they come) after a yāʾ with a sukūn or a kasrah. When a sākin separates (the letters of أَكْهَر and the kasrah)…

# Commentary

Al-Kisāʾī will also not have imālah in the letters of (وَأَكْهَرٍ) أَكْهَر i.e. the hamzah, the kāf, the hāʾ and the rāʾ, with two conditions:

1) They should not come after a yāʾ sākinah (لَا عَنْ سُكُونِ يَا) e.g. خَطِيٓئَةً, كَهَيْئَةِ, الٔاَِيْكَةِ, كَبِيَرةْ.

2) They should not come after a kasrah (عَنْ كَسْرَةٍ) e.g. فِئَةٌ, المَلَآئِكَة, ءَالِهَةً, الآِخِرَةُ.

Thus, if the letters of أَكْهَر come after a yāʾ sākinah or a kasrah, al-Kisāʾī will have imālah in it. However, if أَكْهَر comes after a fatḥah,[234] alif or wāw sākinah e.g. اِمْرَأَةٌ, بَرَآءَةٌ, مَكَّةَ, الشَوْكَةِ, سَفَاهَةٍ, حَسْرَةّ, الحِجَارَةِ, then al-Kisāʾī will have fatḥ.

Thereafter, the author discusses when a sākin letter separates them (وَسَاكِنٌ إِنْ فَصَلَا) i.e. it comes between the letters of أَكْهَر and the kasrah. This continues in the next line.

[234] The letters of أَكْهَر will not come after a ḍammah.

(If another letter separates the letters of أَكْهَر and the kasrah) it does not prevent (imālah). In فِطْرَتَ there is a choice (of imālah and fatḥ). And some (consider the letters) ‚أَهْ‛ (to be) like the 10 (previously-mentioned letters); or imālah is made (before all the letters) except (in) the alif.

# Commentary

If another letter separates the letters of أَكْهَر and the kasrah, then it will not prevent imālah from taking place (لَيْسَ بِحَاجِزٍ) e.g. وِجْهَةٌ, عِبْرَةٌ. However, in فِطْرَتَ of Sūrat al-Rūm: 30, there is difference of opinion (اخْتُلِفْ): both imālah and faṭh are allowed here.

Some (وَالْبَعْضُ) consider the hamzah and the hāʾ (أَهْ) to be like the 10 letters mentioned in the first line – خُصّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ and حَاعَ – i.e. no imālah will take place in them, irrespective of whether they are preceded by a kasrah, yāʾ sākinah or not.

Imālah (يُمَالُ) is also related for al-Kisāʾī if any of the letters come before the hāʾ al-taʾnīth, except for the alif (أَوْ غَيْرْ الٔاَِلِفْ). The instruction for imālah comes at the start of the next line (يُمَالُ).
[Imālah is made (before all the letters) except (in) the alif]; what is preferred is what was mentioned previously. And some relate for Ḥamzah exactly like him (al-Kisāʾī).

# Commentary

Two basic practices have been outlined:

1) Imālah made in فَجَثَتْ زَيْنَبُ لِذَوْدِ شَمْسٍ and أَكْهَر when preceded by a kasrah or yāʾ sākinah, while no imālah is made in خُصّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ and حَاعٍ. Some have added the hamzah and the hāʾ (أَهْ) to this category.

2) Imālah made in all the letters besides the alif.

In this line, Ibn al-Jazarī gives preference (وَالُمخْتَارُ) to the first practice (مَا تَقَدَّمَا).[235]

In the second half of the line, it is mentioned that some (وَالْبَعْضُ) relate from Ḥamzah (عَنْ حَمْزَةَ) the exact differences mentioned here for al-Kisāʾī (مِثْلُهُ).

Their Practices regarding the Rāʾāt

Ziyādāt al-Ṭayyibah:

Via the Shāṭibiyyah, Warsh via al-Azraq has tarqīq in the following:

1) ذِكْرَكَ of Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 4.

2) وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ wherever it comes and وِزْرَكَ of Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 2.

3) حِذْرَكُم of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 71, 102.

4) مِرَآءً of Sūrat al-Kahf: 22.

5) اِفْتِرَآءً عَلَى اللِه of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 140 and اِفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 138.

6) تَنْتَصِرَانِ of Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 35.

7) لَسَاحِرَانِ of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 63.

8) طَهِّرَا بَيْتِي of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 125.

9) وَعَشِيَرتْكُم of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 24. It is restricted to Sūrat al-Tawbah to exclude عَشِيَرتْهُم of Sūrat al-Mujādalah.

10) سِرَاعًا of Sūrah Qāf: 44.

11) ذِرَاعَيْهِ of Sūrat al-Kahf: 18.

12) ذِرَاعًا of Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah: 32.

13) فَعَلَيّ إِجْرَامِي of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام: 35.

14) كِبْرَهُ of Sūrat al-Nūr: 11.

15) لَعِبْرَةً wherever it comes.

16) بِشَرَرٍ of Sūrat al-Mursalāt: 32.

17) حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُم of Sūrat al-Nisā: 90.

Via the Ṭayyibah, tafkhīm will also be allowed in these words for al-Azraq.

Via the Shāṭibiyyah, Warsh via al-Azraq has tafkhīm in إِرَمَ of Sūrat al-Fajr: 7 and بِالْعَشِيّ وَالْإَشْرَاق of Sūrah Ṣād: 18. Via the Ṭayyibah, tarqīq will also be allowed in these two words.

Generally, in the rāʾ maftūḥah munawwanah, Warsh via al-Azraq has difference of opinion, whether the rāʾ is preceded by a kasrah in the same word, e.g. شَاكِرًا, خَضِرًا, صَابِرًا, نَاصِرًا, سَامِرًا, ظَاهِرًا; whether the rāʾ munawwanah and the kasrah are separated by another letter e.g. ذِكْرًا, إِمْرًا, سِتْرًا, وِزْرًا, حِجْرًا, صِهْرًا; where the rāʾ is preceded by a yāʾ līn e.g. خَيْرًا, سَيْرًا, طَيْرًا; or whether the rāʾ is preceded by a yāʾ maddiyyah e.g. قَدِيرًا, كَثِيرًا, كَبِيرًا, etc. He has three practices:

1) Tarqīq of the rāʾ during waṣl and waqf.

2) Tafkhīm of the rāʾ during waṣl and waqf.

3) Tafkhīm of the rāʾ during waṣl, but not during waqf.

The first is related via the Shāṭibiyyah. The Ṭayyibah additionally has numbers two and three.

Via the Shāṭibiyyah, whatever Warsh via al-Azraq applies to the rāʾ maftūḥah – its prerequisites and its differences – will apply to the rāʾ maḍmūmah in reading it with tarqīq. Thus, if the rāʾ maḍmūmah is preceded by a kasrah in the same word, it will be read with tarqīq e.g. خَاسِرُوِنَ, كَافِرُونَ, يَنْتَصِرُونَ, المُدَّثِّرُ, يَغْفِرُ, يَقْدِرُ, السَّاحِرُ, السَّرَآّئِرُ. Likewise, it will be read with tarqīq when it is preceded by a yāʾ sākinah in the same word e.g. غَيْرُهُ, سِيرُوا, كَبِيرُهُم, أَسَاطِيرُ; when it is munawwan preceded by a kasrah in the same word e.g. شَاكِرٌ, مُنْفَطِرٌ, كَافِرٌ; when it is munawwan preceded by a yāʾ sākinah in the same word e.g. خَيْرٌ, خَبِيرٌ, قَدِيرٌ, حَرِيرٌ; when the rāʾ and the kasrah are separated by another letter e.g. ذِكْرَكُم, عِشْرُونَ, بِكْرٌ, ذِكْرُ, سِحْرٌ, الِّذكْرُ. Via the Ṭayyibah, the rāʾ maḍmūmah may also be read with tafkhīm.

Via the Ṭayyibah, those who relate tarqīq in the rāʾ maḍmūmah have difference of opinion in كِبْرٌ مَّا هُمْ بِبَالِغِيهِ of Sūrah Ghāfir: 56 and عِشْرُونَ of Sūrat al-Anfāl: 65. Though they apply tarqīq in the rāʾ maḍmūmah, they will read it with tafkhīm in these two words. Others will read these two words with tarqīq, generally applying tarqīq in all the rāʾ’s that are maḍmūmah.

[235] Al-Nashr: 2/86.
Apply tarqīq (in) the rāʾ (maftūḥah) after the sukūn of a yāʾ or a kasrah (when) in one word for al-Azraq.

# Commentary

The rāʾ being referred to in this line – ‚وَالرَّاءَ‛ – is the rāʾ maftūḥah since the rāʾ maḍmūmah and maksūrah are discussed later in this chapter.

If the rāʾ maftūḥah (وَالرَّاءَ) comes after a yāʾ sākinah (عَنْ سُكُونِ يَاءٍ) or a kasrah (أَوْ كَسْرَةٍ) in one word (مِنْ كِلْمَةٍ), then it will be read with tarqīq (رَقِّقِ) by Warsh via al-Azraq (لِلْأَزْرَقِ) e.g. خَيْرَاتٌ, الخَيْرَ, وَبِالْآِخِرَةِ, لِيَغْفِرَ لَكَ اللُه.

With the stipulation that it should be in the same word (مِنْ كِلْمَةٍ), examples like فِيْ رَيْبِ, بِرَسُولٍ, بِرَبِّكَ and لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ are excluded since the yāʾ sākinah and the kasrah before the rāʾ are in different words.

The remaining Qurrāʾ – including al-Aṣbahānī – will read it with tafkhīm.
He (al-Azraq) does not deem the sākin (between the kasrah and the rāʾ) to prevent (tarqīq of the rāʾ), except the ṭāʾ, the ṣād and the qāf, based on what he (previously) stipulated.

# Commentary

A sākīn letter between the kasrah and the rāʾ would not prevent tarqīq of the rāʾ (وَلَمْ يَرَ السَّاكِنَ فَصْلًا) e.g. إِكْرَاهَ, إِجْرَامِي, عِبْرَةً, الشِّعْرَ, ذِكْرَكَ, إِخْرَاجًا.

However, the sākin letter should not be a ṭāʾ, a ṣād or a qāf (غَيْرَ طَا وَالصَّادِ وَالْقَافِ). If it is one of these three letters, then the rāʾ will be read with tafkhīm e.g. فِطْرَتَ اللِه, إِصْرِهُم, قِطْرًا, إِصْرًا, مِصْرَ, مِصْرًا, وِقْرًا.[236]

By ‚عَلَىٰ مَا اشْتَرَطَا‛ (based on what he – al-Azraq – previously stipulated): the kasrah should be in the same word.

In what follows, some exceptions are mentioned.

[236] Only four of the seven letters of istiʿlāʾ will come as a separator (fāṣil) between the rāʾ and the kasrah: the ṭāʾ, the ṣād, the qāf and the khāʾ.
Certainly apply tarqīq in بِشَرَرٍ(كَالْقَصْرِ) for most. Apply tafkhīm (in) foreign words, along with (tafkhīm in those words) where it (the rāʾ) is repeated.

# Commentary

In (بِشَرَرٍ) بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ of Sūrat al-Mursalāt: 32 most (لِلٔاَكْثَرِ) have tarqīq of the first rāʾ (وَرَقِّقَنْ). Others relate tafkhīm in it for al-Azraq.[237]

Foreign words (وَالٔاَِعْجْمِي) will be read with tafhīm (فَخِّمْ) by al-Azraq e.g. إِبْرَاهِيم, إِسْرَائِيل, عِمْرَان.[238] Similarly, the rāʾ will also be read with tafkhīm in those words in which the rāʾ is repeated (مَعَ المُكَرَّرِ) e.g. ضِرَارًا, فِرَارًا, الفِرَارُ, مِدْرَارًا, إِسْرَارًا. These are the only examples of this in the Qurʾān.

[237] During waqf on بِشَرَرٍ, those who have tarqīq will read the second rāʾ with tarqīq as well, and those who relate tafkhīm will read the second rāʾ with tafkhīm.

[238] In spite of the rāʾ maftūḥah being separated from the kasrah by a letter which is not a ṭāʾ, a ṣād or a qāf, it will still be read with tafkhīm because these words are foreign.
(Tafkhīm in) the likes of سِتْرًا, excluding صِهْرًا in (the opinion of) most. There is an option (of tafkhīm or tarqīq in) حَيْرَانَ, ذِكْرَكَ, إِرَمَ…

# Commentary

This line initially discusses six words that are munawwan and have a letter separating the rāʾ and the kasrah: ذِكْرًا of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 200, إِمْرًا of Sūrat al-Kahf: 71, سِتْرًا of Sūrat al-Kahf: 90, وِزْرًا of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 100, حِجْرًا of Sūrat al-Furqān: 22 and صِهْرًا of Sūrat al-Furqān: 54.

The author refers to these six words when he states ‚وَنَحْوَ سِتْرًا‛, the likes of سِتْرًا.

Most (فِي الٔاَِتَمْ) have tafkhīm in these words, excluding (غَيْرَ صِهْرًا) صِهْرًا in which they will have tarqīq. Others relate tafkhīm in all six words while tarqīq in all six words is also related. The Shāṭibiyyah allows both tafkhīm and tarqīq in these words.

From the second half of the line, 17 words are mentioned in which Warsh via al-Azraq has an option of tafkhīm and tarqīq (وَخُلْفُ). Three are mentioned in rest of this line:

1) حَيْرَانَ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 71.

2) ذِكْرَكَ of Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 4.

3) إِرَمَ of Sūrat al-Fajr: 7.

The others are mentioned in the verses that follow.

(An option of tafkhīm and tarqīq in) وِزْرَ, حِذْرَكُم, مِرَآءً, اِفْتِرَآءً, تَنْتَصِرَانِ, سَاحِرَانِ, طَهِّرَا, عَشِيرَةُ of (Sūrat) al-Tawbah, with سِرَاعًا, and with ذِرَاعَيْهِ, then say ذِرَاعًا.

# Commentary

4) وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ wherever it comes and وِزْرَكَ of Sūrat al-Sharḥ: 2 (وِزْرَ).

5) حِذْرَكُم of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 71, 102.

6) مِرَآءً of Sūrat al-Kahf: 22.

7) اِفْتِرَآءً عَلَى اللِه of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 140 and اِفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 138 (وَافْتِرَا).

8) تَنْتَصِرَانِ of Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 35.

9) (سَاحِرَانِ) لَسَاحِرَانِ of Sūrah Ṭāhā: 63.

10) (طَهِّرَا) طَهِّرَا بَيْتِي of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 125.

11) (عَشِيرَةُ التَّوْبَةِ) وَعَشِيَرتْكُم of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 24. It is restricted to Sūrat al-Tawbah to exclude عَشِيَرتْهُم of Sūrat al-Mujādalah in which only tarqīq is allowed.

12) سِرَاعًا of Sūrah Qāf: 44.

13) ذِرَاعَيْهِ of Sūrat al-Kahf: 18 (وَمَعْ ذِرَاعَيْهِ).

14) (فَقُلْ ذِرَاعَا) ذِرَاعًا of Sūrat al-Ḥāqqah: 32.

The remaining three are mentioned in the next line.
(An option of tafkhīm and tarqīq in) إِجْرَامِي, كِبْرَهُ and لَعِبْرَةً. Most (relate), tafkhīm (in) that (rāʾ maftūḥah) which has a tanwīn for him (al-Azraq) during waṣl.

# Commentary

15) (إِجْرَامِ) فَعَلَيّ إِجْرَامِي of Sūrah Hūd عليه السلام: 35.

16) كِبْرَهُ of Sūrat al-Nūr: 11.

17) لَعِبْرَةً wherever it comes.

Thereafter, Ibn al-Jazarī mentions that most (وَجَلْ) relate tafkhīm of that rāʾ maftūḥah which has a tanwīn (تَفْخِيمُ مَا نُوِّنَ) for al-Azraq (عَنْهُ) during waṣl (وَصَلْ). Thus, during waqf, the rāʾ will be read with tarqīq.

Examples of this are presented in the next line.
Like شَاكِرًا, خَيْرًا, خَبِيرًا, خَضِرًا; likewise, some mention (these same differences for al-Azraq) in حَصِرَتْ (صُدُورُهُم).

# Commentary

Most relate tafkhīm of that rāʾ maftūḥah which has a tanwīn for al-Azraq during waṣl only. Examples of this would be those words in which the rāʾ maftūḥah munawwanah is preceded by a kasrah in the same word, as alluded to by Ibn al-Jazarī via شَاكِرًا and خَضِرًا. Consider also: صَابِرًا, نَاصِرًا, سَامِرًا, ظَاهِرًا, حَاضِرًا, طَآئِرًا, عَاقِرًا, مُدْبِرًا, مُبْصِرًا, فَاجِرًا, مُهَاجِرًا, مُبَشِّرًا, مُنْتَصِرًا, مُغَيِّرًا, مُقْتَدِرًا, سِرًّا, مُسْتَقِرًّا. This would also include the aforementioned six words where the rāʾ munawwanah and the kasrah are separated by another letter: ذِكْرًا, إِمْرًا, سِتْرًا, وِزْرًا, حِجْرًا and صِهْرًا. By the example خَيْرًا, Ibn al-Jazarī suggests other words like it, such as سَيْرًا and طَيْرًا; where the rāʾ is preceded by a yāʾ līn. By خَبِيرًا, he alludes to other like examples where the rāʾ is preceded by a yāʾ maddiyyah: قَدِيرًا, كَثِيرًا, كَبِيرًا, بَشِيرًا, نَذِيرًا, بَصِيرًا, وَزِيرًا, عَسِيرًا, صَغِيرًا, وَحَرِيرًا, وَأَسِيرًا, تَقْدِيرًا, تَطْهِيرًا, تَبْذِيرًا, تَفْجِيرًا, تَكْبِيرًا, تَتْبِيرًا, تَدْمِيرًا, تَفْسِيرًا, قَوَارِيرًا, قَمْطَرِيرًا, مَسْتَطِيرًا, زَمْهَرِيرًا, مُنِيرًا.

While this is the opinion of many, some relate tarqīq in all these words during waṣl and waqf, while others relate tafkhīm in them during waṣl and waqf.

Likewise, some have also mentioned (كَذَاكَ بَعْضٌ ذَكَرَا) these same differences for al-Azraq in (وَحَصِرَتْ) حَصِرَتْ صُدُورُهُم of Sūrat al-Nisā: 90; it will be read with tafkhīm during waṣl and with tarqīq during waqf. However, most read it with tarqīq during waqf and waṣl.

Likewise (these differences mentioned for al-Azraq in the rāʾ maftūḥah will apply) in that (rāʾ) with a ḍammah: apply tarqīq (in the rāʾ maḍmūmah) in (that opinion which is) most sound. The option (between tafkhīm or tarqīq) in كِبْرٌ and عِشْرُونَ is clear.

# Commentary

After discussing the rāʾ maftūḥah, the author now starts with the rāʾ maḍmūmah.

According to that which is more sound (في الٔاَِصَحْ), all that is applied to the rāʾ maftūḥah – its prerequisites and its differences – (كَذَاكَ) will apply to the rāʾ maḍmūmah in reading it with tarqīq (رَقِّقْ). Thus, if the rāʾ maḍmūmah is preceded by a kasrah in the same word, it will be read with tarqīq e.g. خَاسِرُوِنَ, كَافِرُونَ, يَنْتَصِرُونَ, المُدَّثِّرُ, يَغْفِرُ, يَقْدِرُ, السَّاحِرُ, السَّرَآّئِرُ. Likewise, it will be read with tarqīq when it is preceded by a yāʾ sākinah in the same word e.g. غَيْرُهُ, سِيرُوا, كَبِيرُهُم, أَسَاطِيرُ; when it is munawwan preceded by a kasrah in the same word e.g. شَاكِرٌ, مُنْفَطِرٌ, كَافِرٌ; when it is munawwan preceded by a yāʾ sākinah in the same word e.g. خَيْرٌ, خَبِيرٌ, قَدِيرٌ, حَرِيرٌ; when the rāʾ and the kasrah are separated by another letter e.g. ذِكْرَكُم, عِشْرُونَ, بِكْرٌ, ذِكْرُ, سِحْرٌ, الِّذكْرُ.

Others would read this rāʾ with tafkhīm.

In the second half of the verse, two words are mentioned in which difference of opinion is related according to those who transmit tarqīq in the rāʾ maḍmūmah (كِبْرٌ) كِبْرٌ مَّا هُمْ بِبَالِغِيهِ:(والْخُلْفُ) of Sūrah Ghāfir: 56 and (وَعِشْرُونَ) عِشْرُونَ of Sūrat al-Anfāl:

65. Though they apply tarqīq in the rāʾ maḍmūmah, they will read these two words with tafkhīm. Others will read these two words with tarqīq, generally applying tarqīq in all the rāʾ’s that are maḍmūmah.

If (the rāʾ) sākinah comes after a kasrah, then every teacher applies tarqīq in it (the rāʾ), o my companion. Wherever a letter of istiʿlāʾ comes after the rāʾ sākinah, then apply tafkhīm (in it). And in (the letter of istiʿlāʾ that) has a kasrah, there is an option, except…

# Commentary

From this verse, the author starts discussing the rāʾ sākinah.

If the rāʾ sākinah (وإنْ تَكُنْ سَاكِنَةً) comes after a kasrah (عَنْ كَسْرِ), then all the Qurrāʾ (كُلّ مُقْرِي) – there is no difference of opinion here – agree that the rāʾ will be read with tarqīq (رَقَّقَهَا) e.g. فِرْعَوْنَ, شِرْعَةً, لَشِرْذِمَةٌ, تُنْذِرْهُم, أُحْصِرْتُمَ, وَاصْبِرْ.

In the second line, an exception to the rule is mentioned. Wherever a letter of istiʿlāʾ comes after the rāʾ sākinah (وَحَيْثُ جَاءَ بَعْدُ حَرْفُ اسْتِعْلَا), then it will be read with tafkhīm (فَخِّمْ) e.g. قِرْطَاسٍ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 7, فِرْقَةٍ of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 122, وَإِرْصَادًا of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 107, مِرْصَادًا of Sūrat al-Nabaʾ: 21 and لَبِالْمِرْصَادِ of Sūrat al-Fajr: 14.

The student of Ibn al-Jazarī, Sheikh al-Nuwayrī, stipulates that the letter of istiʿlāʾ should be in the same word as the rāʾ sākinah (مُتَّصِل) and there should not be an alif separating the rāʾ sākinah and the letter of istiʿlāʾ.[239] The first stipulation is general and will exclude وَلَا تُصَعِّرْ خَدَّكَ of Sūrah Luqmān: 18, فَاصْبِرْ صَبْرًا of Sūrat al-Maʿārij: 5, أَنْذِرْ قَوْمَكَ of Sūrah Nūḥ عليه السلام: 1, according to all the Qirāʾāt.[240]

The second stipulation of al-Nuwayrī is specific to the narration of Warsh via al-Azraq when the rāʾ is maftūḥah; it will exclude هٰذَا فِرَاقُ of Sūrat al-Kahf: 78, الفِرَاقُ of Sūrat al-Qiyāmah: 28, بِالْعَشِيّ وَالْإَشْرَاق of Sūrah Ṣād: 18, إِعْرَاضًا of Sūrat al-Nisāʾ: 128, عَلَيْكَ إِعْرَاضُهُم of Sūrat al-Anʿām: 35.

However, if the letter of istiʿlāʾ after the rāʾ sākinah – or following an alif after the rāʾ maftūḥah – has a kasrah (وَفِي ذِي الْكَسْرّ), then there is an option of tafkhīm or tarqīq in the rāʾ (خُلْفٌ). This is only found in فِرْقٍ of Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ: 63 and الاَِشْرَاقِ of Sūrah Ṣād: 18.

At the end of the line, one exception is hinted at. It continues into the next line.

[239] Sharḥ Ṭayyibat al-Nashr of al-Nuwayrī: 2/26.

[240] Specific to the narration of Warsh via al-Azraq, if the rāʾ maftūḥah or maḍmūmah is followed by a letter of istiʿlāʾ in a separate word, then the rāʾ will still be read with tarqīq e.g. لِتُنْذِرَ قَوْمًا of Sūrah Yāsīn: 6, الِّذكْرَ صَفْحًا of Sūrat al-Zukhruf: 5, الْمُدَّثِّرُ * قُمْ of Sūrat al-Muddath-thir: 1-2.
[Except in] صِرَاطِ. It is correct from all (the Qurrāʾ) that tafkhīm be made (in) الْمَرْءِ and the likes of مَرْيَم.

# Commentary

If the letter of istiʿlāʾ following the rāʾ has a kasrah, then one has an option between reading it with tafkhīm or tarqīq for Warsh via al-Azraq. However, the word إِلَّا) صِرَاطِ صِرَاطِ) is an exception to this: though the ṭāʾ has a kasrah, it will only be read with tafkhīm wherever it appears in the Qurʾān.

Thereafter, a matter in which all the Qurrāʾ – including Warsh via al-Azraq – agree upon is mentioned. It is correct (وَالصَّوَابُ) according to all the Qurrāʾ (عَنْ كُلّ) that tafkhīm be made (أَنْ يُفَخَّمَا) in الْمَرْءِ of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 102 and Sūrat al-Anfāl: 24, as well as the likes of (وَنَحْوُ مَرْيَمَا) مَرْيَم wherever it comes. By stating ‚وَنَحْوُ مَرْيَمَا‛ (the likes of Maryam), other words in which the rāʾ sākinah is followed by a yāʾ meant e.g. القَرْيَة. Thus, even though some books, like that of Makkī ibn Abī Ṭālib, al-Ahwāzī, amongst others, mention tarqīq in the rāʾ sākinah when followed by a kasrah or yāʾ sākinah, the practice of all is to read these words with tafkhīm.

[If the rāʾ sākinah] comes after a circumstantial kasrah, or (the rāʾ sākinah comes after a kasrah in) a separate (word), then apply tafkhīm (in the rāʾ). If you apply rawm (on the rāʾ during waqf), then (the rāʾ will be recited) as you would during waṣl.

# Commentary

If the rāʾ sākinah comes after a circumstantial kasrah (وَبَعْدَ كَسْرٍ عَارِضٍ), whether it’s a temporary hamzah e.g. اِرْجِعِي, اِمْرَأَة, or whether it’s due to two sākin letters coming together e.g. أَمِ ارْتَابُوا, لِمَنِ ارْتَضَىٰ, إِنِ ارْتَبْتُم, the rāʾ will be read with tafkhīm (فَخِّمْ).

Similarly, if the rāʾ sākinah comes after a kasrah which is in a separate word (أَوْ مُنْفَصِلْ) e.g. رَبّ ارْجِعُون, رَبّ ارْحَمْهُمَا, then the rāʾ will be read with tafkhīm (فَخِّمْ).

If rawm is being made on the rāʾ during waqf (وَإِنْ تَرُمْ), then the rāʾ will be recited as it is during waṣl (فَمِثْلَ مَا تَصِلْ). So in words like الكِبَرِ and وَالْفَجْرِ, all the Qurrāʾ will read the rāʾ with tarqīq when applying rawm. In words like يَقْدِرُ and خَبِيرٌ, all besides Warsh via al-Azraq will have tafkhīm in the rāʾ, considering al-Azraq’s previously-mentioned applications.

Apply tarqīq in the rāʾ if you are making imālah, or if the rāʾ has a kasrah. And in (the rāʾ) with a sukūn during waqf, apply tafkhīm; and support (this view), except when it comes after a yāʾ sākinah, or a kasrah, or tarqīq (of the rāʾ) or imālah.

# Commentary

If imālah is being made in the rāʾ (إنْ تُمَلْ) then it should be read with tarqīq (وَرَقِّقِ الرَّا) e.g. ذِكْرَىٰ, بُشْرَىٰ, أَسْرَىِٰ.

Thereafter, the rāʾ maksūrah is discussed (أوْ تُكْسَرّ); it will be read with tarqīq (وَرَقِّقِ الرَّا) by all the Qurrāʾ e.g. رِزْقٍ, فَارِضٌ, وَبِالزُّبُرِ.

If the rāʾ is read with a sukūn during waqf (وَفِي سُكُونِ الْوَقْفِ), then generally[241] it will be read with tafkhīm (فَخِّمْ), except when it comes after a yāʾ sākinah (مَا لَمْ تَكُنْ مِنْ بَعْدِ يَا سَاكِنَةِ) e.g. لَا ضَيْرَ, وَالْحَمِيرَ; or comes after a kasrah (أَوْ كَسْرٍ) e.g. كُفِرَ, ذِكْرٌ; or after a rāʾ muraqqaqah i.e. بِشَرَرٍ according to al-Azraq; or after imālah e.g. وِبِالْأِسْحْارِ, الٔاَِبْرَارِ. Thus, during waqf, the rāʾ will be full inالقَمَرُ, التَّكَاثُرُ, القَدْرِ, خُسْرّ, الٔانْهَارُ, الٔاُِمُورُ.

Abū Bakr ibn al-Jazarī, explains that by his father stating ‚وَانْصُرِ‛ (assist this view), he refutes the opinion that when stopping on a rāʾ maksūrah, one can only stop with tarqīq.[242] The Lāmāt

Ziyādāt al-Ṭayyibah:

According to the Shāṭibiyyah, Warsh via al-Azraq will have taghlīṭḥ of the lām maftūḥah when it is preceded by a ṭāʾ maftūḥah, ṭḥāʾ maftūḥah, ṭāʾ sākinah or ṭḥāʾ sākinah e.g. الطَّلَاقُ, وَانْطَلَقَ, وَبَطَلَ, ظَلَمَ, بِظَلَّامٍ, ظَلّ, مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ, أَظْلَمَ. Via the Ṭayyibah, tarqīq of the lām is also allowed in these lāms for Warsh via al-Azraq.[243]

According to the Shāṭibiyyah, Warsh via al-Azraq has tarqīq in the first lām of صَلْصَالٍ in Sūrat al-Ḥijr: 26, 28, 33 and Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 14. Via the Ṭayyibah, he will also have taghlīṭḥ of the lām.

Warsh via al-Aṣbahānī will read like Qālūn in all these lāms.

[241] Though Ibn al-Jazarī encourages the practice of tafkhīm in general, there are specific places where he has given other preferences e.g. عَيْنْ الْقِطْرِ of Sūrah Sabaʾ: 12, مِصْرَ of Sūrah Yūsuf عليه السلام: 99, يَسْرّ of Sūrat al-Fajr: 4.

[242] Sharḥ Ṭayyibat al-Nashr of Abū Bakr ibn al-Jazarī: 139.

[243] The Shāṭibiyyah and the Ṭayyibah agree regarding their rules pertaining to the lām maftūḥah when it is preceded by a ṣād maftūḥah or ṣād sākinah. 354
Al-Azraq makes taghlīṭḥ of the lām with a fatḥah (when it) comes after the sukūn of a ṣād, ṭāʾ or ṭḥāʾ.

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq (وَأَزْرَقٌ) with have taghlīṭḥ (غَلَّظَا) of the lām with a fatḥah (لِفَتْحِ لَامٍ) when it comes after a ṣād, ṭāʾ or ṭḥāʾ (صَادٍ أوْ طَاءٍ وَظَا) that have a sukūn (بَعْدَ سَكُونِ) e.g. يَصْلَىٰ, سَيَصْلَىٰ, اِصْلَوْهَا, مِنْ أَصْلَابِكُم, إِصْلَاحًا, فَصْلَ الْخِطَابِ, مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ, أَظْلَمَ, يُظْلَمُونَ.

Or when it’s (the ṣād, ṭāʾ or ṭḥāʾ) fatḥah. There is an option (between taghlīṭḥ or tarqīq) if there is an alif in it (between the lām maftūḥah and the ṣād, ṭāʾ or ṭḥāʾ), or imālah is made, (or an option in the lām) with is sākin because of waqf.

# Commentary

Warsh via al-Azraq will also have taghlīṭḥ of the lām maftūḥah when the ṣād, ṭāʾ or ṭḥāʾ before it has a fatḥah (أَوْ فَتْحِهَا) e.g. الصَّلَوٰةَ, صَلَحَ, مُفَصَّلًا, صَلَّىٰ, يُصَلَّبُوا, الطَّلَاقُ, وَانْطَلَقَ, أَطَّلَعَ, وَبَطَلَ, مُعَطَّلَةٍ, طَلَبًا, وُالْمُطَلَّقَاتُ, طَلَّقْتُم, ظَلَمَ, بِظَلَّامٍ, ظَلّ.

There is an option between taghlīṭḥ and tarqīq (اخْتُلِفْ) if an alif (أَلِفْ) is placed (وَإنْ يَحُلْ) between the lām maftūḥah and one of these three letters e.g. فِصَالًا, يَصَّالَحَا, طَالَ, أَفَطَالَ, فَطَالَ.

There is also an option between taghlīṭḥ and tarqīq (اخْتُلِفْ) if imālah (أَوْ إِنْ يُمَلْ) takes place in the alif after the lām maftūḥah e.g. صَلَّىٰ, يَصْلَىٰ, يَصْلَىٰهَا.

There is also an option between taghlīṭḥ and tarqīq (اخْتُلِفْ) if the lām maftūḥah is read as sākin due to waqf (مَعْ سَاكِنِ الْوَقْفِ) e.g. أَنْ يُوصَلَ, وَبَطَلَ, ظَلّ, وَفَصْلَ.
(An option between taghlīṭḥ or tarqīq) is (also) related by the ṭāʾ and the ṭḥāʾ; the more sound (opinion) is its (the lām’s) tafkhīm. The opposite (i.e. tarqīq) is preponderant in the verse-ends.

# Commentary

An option of taghlīṭḥ and tarqīq is also related by the ṭāʾ and the ṭḥāʾ (وَقِيلَ عِنْدَ الطَّاءِ وَالظَّا); the more sound opinion (والٔاَِصَحْ) is tafkhīm of the lām maftūḥah (تَفْخِيُمهَا) by the ṭāʾ and ṭḥāʾ.

The opposite (وَالْعَكْسُ) i.e. tarqīq, is preponderant (رَجَحْ) by the verse-ends (فِي الآِيِ) e.g. وَلَا صَلَّىٰ of Sūrat al-Qiyāmah: 31, فَصَلَّىٰ of Sūrat al-Aʿlāʾ: 15, وَإِذَا صَلَّىٰ of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq:

10. Note that in these three places only tarqīq with taqlīl will be allowed.
Likewise (tarqīq is preferred) in صَلْصَالٍ. All (views) besides what I mentioned, are anomalous. And the name of Allah, all apply tafkhīm (in it)…

# Commentary

Likewise (كَذَاكَ), tarqīq will also be preferred in the first lām of صَلْصَالٍ in Sūrat al-Ḥijr: 26, 28, 33 and Sūrat al-Raḥmān: 14.

All other views besides what Ibn al-Jazarī has mentioned here (غَيْرُ مَا ذَكَرْتُ) should be considered as anomalous (وَشَذّ).[244]

All the Qurrāʾ (كُلّ) will have tafkhīm (فَخَّمَا) of the lām in the name of Allah (وَاسْمَ اللِه) when followed by a fatḥah or a ḍammah. This continues into the next line.

[244] For example, the author of al-Kāfī, Ibn Shurayḥ, relates taghlīṭḥ of the lām maḍmūmah after a ṣād or a ṭḥāʾ e.g. فَصْلٌ, مَظْلُومًا.
[All apply tafkhīm in it] after a fatḥah or a ḍammah. And there is an option (of tafkhīm or tarqīq) after (a letter) in which imālah takes place; no (option) is described after (a letter of) tarqīq.

# Commentary

All the Qurrāʾ will have tafkhīm of the lām in the name of Allah when followed by a fatḥah or a ḍammah (مِنْ بَعْدِ فَتْحَةٍ وَضَمّ) e.g. اَلُله, رَسُولُ اللِه. The implied opposite is that after a kasrah it will be read with tarqīq e.g. بِالِله.

If the lām of Allah comes after a letter in which imālah takes place (بَعْدَ مُمَالٍ), then there is an option between tafkhīm and tarqīq of the lām (واخْتُلِفْ). This is found in the narration of al-Sūsī: نَرَى اللَه of Sūrat al-Baqarah: 55 and وَسَيَرَى اللُه of Sūrat al-Tawbah: 94.

There is no difference of opinion (لَا) ascribed (وُصِفْ) to when it comes after a rāʾ muraqqaqah (مُرَقَّقٍ) in the narration of Warsh via al-Azraq e.g. أَفَغَيْرَ اللِه, يُبَشِّرُ اللُه, وَلَذِكْرُ اللِه أَكْبَرُ. The lām here will be read with tafkhīm in spite of the rāʾ muraqqaqah before it.[245] Waqf upon the Last Letter

This chapter discusses the various ways of stopping based upon the ḥarakah on the last letter.

[245] This is particularly mentioned due to some who have a tendency of reading the rāʾ muraqqaqah with imālah instead. See al-Nashr: 2/117.
The primary (way) in waqf is (with) a sukūn. Certainly apply ishmām and rawm in the rafʿ and ḍammah for them (the Qurrāʾ).

# Commentary

From amongst the ways of making waqf, the primary manner (وَالٔاَِصْلُ فِي الوَقْفِ) is with a sukūn (السُّكُونُ). Since ibtidāʾ is only possible with a ḥarakah, the primary manner of waqf – which is the opposite of ibtidāʾ – is with a sukūn i.e. removing the ḥarakah (iskān).

In rafʿ (nominative case) and ḍammah (فِي الرَّفْعِ وَالضَّمّ), the Qurrāʾ (وَلَهُمْ) also have ishmām (اشْمِمَنَّهُ) and rawm (ورُمْ) e.g. وَرَبُّكَ الْأِكْرَمُ, نَسْتَعِيُنْ, خَيْرٌ.

The difference between rafʿ and ḍammah is that the former indicates towards that which is declinable (muʿrab) while the latter indicates to that which is indeclinable (mabnī).
Prevent both of them (rawm and ishmām) in the naṣb and fatḥah, but in the jarr and the kasrah, rawm is made generally.

# Commentary

Rawm and ishmām are not allowed on a fatḥah and on a naṣb (وَامْنَعْهُمَا فِي النَّصْبِ وَالْفَتْحِ) e.g. خَلَقَ, العَالَمِيَنْ, خَيْرَ.

The difference between naṣb (accusative case) and fatḥah is that the former indicates towards that which is declinable (muʿrab) while the latter indicates to that which is indeclinable (mabnī).

Rawm is allowed on a kasrah and jarr (بَلَىٰ فِي الْجَرّ وَالْكَسْرِ يُرَامُ مُسْجَلَا) e.g. بِالْقَلَمِ, الرَّحِيِم, شَيْءٍ.

The difference between jarr (genitive case) and kasrah is that the former indicates towards that which is declinable (muʿrab) while the latter indicates to that which is indeclinable (mabnī).
Rawm is bring a part of the ḥarakah; their ishmām is an indication with not ḥarakah.

# Commentary

This line defines rawm and ishmām.

Rawm means to read the ḥarakah partially (وَالرَّوْمُ الاَتْيَانُ بِبَعْضِ الحَرَكَهْ).[246] Due to it being read partially, its sound is weakened or lowered due to the shortening of its timing; those close by are able to hear it.[247] Ishmām is an indication to a ḍammah (إِشْمَامُهُمْ إِشَارَةٌ) soon after reciting the sukūn; there is no ḥarakah read when applying ishmām (لَا حَرَكَهْ).

[246] Ikhtilās shares this definition. However, ikhtilās differs from rawm in the following: 1) Ikhtilās is allowed on all three ḥarakāt e.g. أَرِنَا, يَهَدِّيْ, يَأْمُرَكُم. 2) Ikhtilās is not restricted to waqf. 3) In ikhtilās, most of the ḥarakah remains (two-thirds of the ḥarakah remains) while in rawm most of the ḥarakah is lost (one-third of the ḥarakah is maintained).

[247] Sharḥ Ṭayyibat al-Nashr of al-Nuwayrī: 2/47.
Transmissions are related (regarding rawm and ishmām) from Abū ʿAmr and the Kufis; and (rawm and ishmām) is a chosen practice linked to all the Qurrāʾ.

# Commentary
